finding.summary: FDX3 cancellation must distinguish stopping future iterator consumption from preempting an already-running TTS inference unit. The existing benchmark already drives both engines through iterator next() boundaries. Upstream/reference APIs are generator/iterable shaped, but that shape alone does not prove hard mid-inference cancellation. The first system discriminator should therefore make sink-delivery fencing and packet commit fencing authoritative, and promote producer-generation cancellation only when an explicit internal cancel/close boundary is actually executed and traced.
finding.kokoro_exact_project_observation: The exact F2 benchmark calls pipeline(segment, ...) and repeatedly next(iterator), recording generated audio only after each result is yielded. It does not invoke an engine-specific cancellation API.
finding.piper_exact_project_observation: The exact F2 benchmark calls iter(voice.synthesize(segment)) and repeatedly next(iterator), recording each returned audio chunk. It does not invoke an engine-specific cancellation API.
finding.upstream_reference_observation: Current upstream Kokoro examples expose KPipeline output as a Generator consumed result-by-result. Piper 1.7.0 provenance binds the project pin to OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl commit 7b8e8f7197a480047677715f00d3d78903b55a2a; Piper reference implementations synthesize/yield bounded audio units rather than establishing an external hard-preemption contract.
finding.non_inference: Generator/iterator structure is not evidence that the model call currently computing the next result can be forcibly cancelled. Do not mint producer_cancel credit from iterator close, loop break, task cancellation, or sink rejection unless the exact pinned runtime trace proves what computation stopped.

primary_external_evidence.observation: generate_audio is a Generator and yield-from consumes KPipeline results; save path iterates result-by-result.
piper-tts 1.7.0 is attested to OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl commit 7b8e8f7197a480047677715f00d3d78903b55a2a.

acceptance_split.sink_delivery_cancel_credit: May promote at bounded headless scope when zero interrupted-packet chunks are sink-admitted after the causal sink cancel boundary, with any preaccepted buffer separately measured.
acceptance_split.packet_commit_fence_credit: May promote when the interrupted VoiceOutputPacket is terminal and commit_eligible=false and cannot own durable heard/result/tool state.
acceptance_split.producer_generation_cancel_credit: Remains zero unless exact pinned runtime execution proves an internal producer stop/preemption boundary beyond merely ceasing iterator consumption.

latency_guidance.reason: Each clock covers a different boundary and only the last requires physical output evidence.

explicit_zero_credit: whole voice system until composed d622 execution passes
next_exact_action: Let the already-running exact Kokoro/Piper S1 discriminator terminalize without duplicate dispatch. If at least one existing engine yields valid real local audio, reuse that exact accepted engine inside the existing d622 owner-VPS FDX2/FDX3/FDX4/FDX6 execution and emit separate producer, sink and packet-fence cancellation fields. Do not block a bounded sink/packet FDX3 pass solely because hard internal producer preemption is absent, and do not mint producer-cancel credit unless it is truly executed.
